aspect: Isolated incidents generally do not qualify
description: Petty slights, annoyances and isolated incidents are not actionable unless extremely serious. The conduct must be severe or pervasive enough that a reasonable person would find the environment hostile.

aspect: Which requires the target to keep a tally
description: Because the threshold is cumulative, the sensible response is to document everything - dates, words, witnesses - while continuing to work alongside the person being documented.
energy_note: Keeping a file on a colleague, for two years, in secret.

aspect: It can come from clients and customers too
description: Conduct by non-employees under the employer's control counts, and the employer is liable where it knew or should have known and failed to act - which in practice means somebody must report the customer who tips well.
energy_note: The regular who is good for business.

description: Individually: a comment about her dress in March, a hand on her back in May, a joke in July, being asked to sit next to a client in September because 'he likes you'. Her note-keeping app has eleven entries. Her solicitor says it is probably still not enough.
energy_note: Eleven entries, and probably still not enough.
